study: Author of the study. Formated as: Last name of first author, year
condition_arm1: Type of treatment (HNC= Helping the Noncompliant Child, NFPP= New Forest Parenting Package, Triple-P= Positive Parenting Program, BPT= behavioural parent training, STEPP= Strategies to Enhance Positive Parenting , DRC= daily report card, Coaches= Coaching Our Acting-out Children: Heightening Essential Skills, PSY= psychoeducation, EGTP= Enhanced Group Triple-P, PCIT= Parent-Child Interaction Therapy, FSS(-EE)= Family-School Success(-Early Education), CLS= Collaborative Life Skills, CLAS= Child Life and Attention Skills, PFT= parent-focused treatment, WPJ= Well Parent Japan, STAND= Supporting Teens' Academic Needs Daily, PT= parent training, IY= Incredible Years)
condition_arm2: Type of comparator (tau= treatment as usual, wl= waitlist, PC&S= parent counseling and support, CARE= Coping With ADHD Through Relationships and Education)
multi_arm1: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the first arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of parent training interventions, face-to-face and Internet-based, this variable would be set to f2f and Internet, respectively.
multi_arm2: In multiarm trials, this variable provides a specification of the type of treatment used in the second arm. This variable is set to NA (missing) when the study was not a multiarm trial. For example, if a multiarm trial employed two types of control groups, waitlist and placebo, this variable would be set to wl and plac, respectively. Typically, multiarm trials employ two or more active treatments (e.g. CBT and problem-solving therapy), which are compared to the same control group (e.g. a waitlist). This means that values in multi_arm2 do not differ (e.g. they are always wl for this specific multiarm trial); nevertheless, the variable should be specified in the dataset.
instrument: Describes the instrument through which the relevant outcome was measured.
rating: Encodes how the outcome measurement was rated (e.g., parent, teacher, mother, coder).
outcome_category: Broad behavioural outcome category (ADHD total= total ADHD score, ADHD HI= hiperactivity, ADHD A= inattention, behavioural problems= other behavioural problems).
outcome_type: Type of outcome that builds the basis of the comparison, e.g. means and standard deviations (msd), change from baseline, response, remission, other statistics, etc.
Source of participants: Encodes how the participants were recruited (e.g., community, clinic, school).
Country: Country where the trial was carried out
time: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained (e.g. post or follow-up).
time_weeks: The measurement point at which the outcome was obtained, in weeks after randomization. If unspecified, code as NA.
seq_gen: Score on the sequence generation scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
alloc_conce: Score on the allocation concealment scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
blindind_assess: Score on the blinding of assessors scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
missing_data: Score on the dealing with missing data scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
vested_int: Score on the vested interest scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
selec_report: Score on the selective reporting scale of the Risk of Bias assessment (0= high risk; 1= low risk; ?= unclear).
d1: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 1: Randomization process (low, some concerns or high)
d2: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 2: Deviations from the intended interventions (low, some concerns or high)
d3: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 3: Missing outcome data (low, some concerns or high)
d4: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 4: Measurement of the outcome (low, some concerns or high)
d5: Risk of bias (tool 2) domain 5: Selection of the reported result (low, some concerns or high)
rob: Overall risk of bias score (low, some concerns or high)
event_arm1: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm
event_arm2: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm
totaln_arm1: Total number of participants arm 1 (event data)
totaln_arm2: Total number of participants arm 2 (event data)
sd_change_arm1: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 1
sd_change_arm2: Standard deviation for the change from baseline arm 2
precalc_g: The pre-calculated value of Hedges' g (small-sample bias corrected standardized mean difference; Hedges, 1981).
precalc_log_rr: The pre-calculated value of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
precalc_log_rr_se: The standard error of the log-risk ratio logeRR, comparing events in the first arm to events in the second arm.
.id: metapsyTools generated variable: Unique identifier for a trial arm comparison/row.
.g: metapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (Hedges' g).
.g_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of Hedges' g.
.log_rr: metapsyTools generated variable: Calculated effect size (logeRR).
.log_rr_se: metapsyTools generated variable: Standard error of logeRR.
.event_arm1: metapsyTools generated variable: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the first trial arm.
.event_arm2: metapsyTools generated variable: Number of events (responders, remission, deterioration cases) in the second trial arm.
.totaln_arm1: metapsyTools generated variable: Total sample size in the first trial arm.
.totaln_arm2: metapsyTools generated variable: Total sample size in the second trial arm.
